- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:2125-2134 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The one-page margin in `snapshot_cap = max(1, min(1000, args.per_page * args.max_pages) - args.per_page)` lowers the threshold from 1000 to 900 at the defaults (per_page=100, max_pages=10). A complete listing of 900-999 runs sets neither `capped` nor `page_limit_reached`, so it keeps its ETag (runs_etag writeback at lines 2283-2288). Every later 304 then triggers a full refetch, on every run, with no end. Also, `--max-pages 1` drops the cap to 1, which turns off snapshot reuse completely.
  WHY: A watched repo in the 900-999 band loses the conditional-request fast path for good, at up to 10 extra page requests per repo per run against a PAT budget that is already limited. Reviewers disagree on severity: minimax_minimax-m3 and openai_gpt-6-luna say MAJOR; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash say NIT. Those two call the impact bounded: it is mostly limited to a fixed `--since` on a quiet repo, and the margin is the best heuristic available because the cache schema has no truncation flag. The highest severity is used here.

  PROBLEM: The one-page margin classifies complete listings of 900-999 runs as possibly partial, because `page_limit_reached` is not set (verified at scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:692-694 and 719-720). The reviewer calls this the best available heuristic.
